preconditions.description: The number of necklace parts n is a positive integer between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= a < 2**20 and 0 <= b < 2**20 for a, b in parts)
preconditions.description: Each necklace part consists of two pearls with colors a and b, where each color is a non-negative integer less than 2^20.
The input contains exactly n necklace parts, where parts is a list of tuples (a, b) representing each part.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is a single integer max_beauty, representing the maximum possible beauty of the necklace, where beauty is defined as the minimum beauty of any connection in the cycle.
The second line of stdout contains exactly 2n distinct integers representing the indices of pearls in the order they appear on the cycle.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= p <= 2 * n for p in pearl_order)
postconditions.description: Each pearl index in the order is between 1 and 2n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(pearl_order.count(i) == 1 for i in range(1, 2 * n + 1))
postconditions.description: Each pearl index from 1 to 2n appears exactly once in the order.

postconditions.expression: all(abs(pearl_order.index(2 * i - 1) - pearl_order.index(2 * i)) == 1 for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For each necklace part i (1-based), the indices of its two pearls (2i-1 and 2i) are adjacent in the order.

The beauty of the constructed necklace (minimum beauty of any connection in the cycle) is at least max_beauty, where beauty of a connection (u, v) is defined as follows: if u == v, beauty is 20; otherwise, beauty is the largest k such that 2^k divides (u XOR v).
There is no valid cycle using all parts with a beauty strictly greater than max_beauty.
